verifyNote: Reference guidance. Letter systems and colours differ by country and by extinguisher make. Always read the label on the extinguisher and follow the site fire plan.

label_systems.label: Europe, Gulf and many countries (EN 2)
label_systems.note: A solids, B liquids, C gases, D metals, F cooking oils and fats. Electrical is not a class: use a non-conductive agent after isolating power.

label_systems.label: USA and Canada (NFPA 10, ULC)
label_systems.note: A ordinary combustibles, B flammable liquids and gases, C energised electrical equipment, D combustible metals, K cooking oils and fats.

label_systems.label: India
label_systems.note: Check the label on the extinguisher. Letters usually follow the European style. Follow the site fire plan and local Fire Service requirements.

fire_types.name: Ordinary combustibles
fire_types.materials: Wood, paper, cardboard, cloth, rubber, many plastics
fire_types.how: Cool the fuel. Water is the best agent.
fire_types.danger: Smouldering inside piles can restart the fire.

fire_types.name: Flammable liquids
fire_types.materials: Petrol, diesel, solvents, paint, oils, alcohol
fire_types.examples: Fuel spill, paint store, oil leak
fire_types.how: Smother the surface. Never use a straight water jet.
fire_types.danger: Burning liquid spreads. Water makes it worse.

fire_types.name: Flammable gases
fire_types.materials: LPG, propane, acetylene, natural gas, hydrogen
fire_types.examples: Gas cylinder or pipeline leak fire
fire_types.how: Stop the gas supply first. Then control the fire.
fire_types.danger: Putting out a leaking gas fire without stopping the leak can cause an explosion.

fire_types.name: Combustible metals
fire_types.materials: Magnesium, aluminium powder, titanium, sodium, lithium metal
fire_types.how: Use only a special dry powder for metals or dry sand.
fire_types.danger: Water, CO2 and ordinary powder can react violently.

fire_types.name: Cooking oils and fats
fire_types.materials: Deep fryer oil, animal fat, vegetable oil
fire_types.how: Use a wet chemical extinguisher. Turn off the heat if safe.
fire_types.danger: Water causes a fireball. Hot oil can reignite.

fire_types.name: Energised electrical equipment
fire_types.how: Isolate power if safe. Use a non-conductive agent.
fire_types.danger: Water or foam on live equipment can electrocute you.

extinguishers.name: Water
extinguishers.label_colour: Red body, plain or red label zone
extinguishers.notes: Cheap and effective on Class A only. Never on live electrics or burning oil.

extinguishers.name: Foam (AFFF / AR-AFFF)
extinguishers.notes: Good for liquid fires. Conducts electricity. Do not use on live equipment.

extinguishers.name: Dry powder ABC
extinguishers.notes: Multi-purpose. Reduces visibility and leaves a corrosive residue. Not good in small closed rooms.

extinguishers.name: Dry powder BC
extinguishers.notes: Fast knock-down on liquid and gas fires. Not rated for Class A.

extinguishers.name: Carbon dioxide (CO2)
extinguishers.notes: Clean, no residue. Short range. Do not hold the metal horn with bare hands: it gets extremely cold. Danger in small closed rooms.

extinguishers.name: Wet chemical
extinguishers.notes: Made for cooking oil fires. Forms a soapy layer on hot oil. Not for live electrics.

extinguishers.name: Special powder for metals (Class D)
extinguishers.notes: Only for metal fires. Needs trained users.

co2.note: Only very small fires. No cooling effect

water.note: Use only to cool cylinders and surroundings

abc.note: Stop the gas first or it may reignite and explode

bc.note: Stop the gas first or it may reignite and explode

powderd.note: Only suitable agent. Dry sand for small amounts

abc.note: Isolate power first. Residue damages equipment

co2.note: Best for sensitive equipment. Isolate power first

pass.detail: Pull the pin and break the tamper seal.
Aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, not the flames.
Sweep side to side across the base until the fire is out.

before_fighting: Raise the alarm first and make sure others are leaving
Fight a fire only if it is small, such as the size of a waste bin, and you have a clear exit behind you
Check the label: is this the right extinguisher for this fire?
Stand 2 to 3 metres back and keep your back to the exit
Stay low if there is smoke and never let the fire get between you and the exit
do_not_fight: The fire is spreading fast or is larger than a waste bin
Smoke is filling the room or you cannot see
You do not know what is burning or which extinguisher to use
The extinguisher is empty, damaged or you are alone with no exit behind you
There are gas cylinders, explosives or hazardous chemicals nearby

race.detail: Help people in immediate danger only if it is safe.
Raise the alarm and call the emergency number.
Close doors and windows to slow the fire and smoke.
Fight a small fire if trained and safe. Otherwise leave and go to the assembly point.

inspection.monthly_note: A quick visual check every month is required by NFPA 10 and by most site fire plans. Record the date, the unit number and your name.

monthly.text: Extinguisher is in its marked place, visible and not blocked
monthly.fail: Move or clear the obstruction and report

monthly.text: Sign or marker above the extinguisher is in place
Safety pin and tamper seal are intact
monthly.fail: Report: it may have been used or tampered with

monthly.text: Pressure gauge needle is in the green zone (stored pressure types)
monthly.fail: Tag out and replace the unit

monthly.text: Body has no dents, rust, leaks or damage
monthly.fail: Tag out and replace the unit

monthly.text: Hose and nozzle are free of cracks, blockages and insects
monthly.fail: Tag out and have it repaired

monthly.text: Label is readable and the correct type for the hazard in this area
monthly.fail: Replace the label or the extinguisher

monthly.text: Service tag shows the last annual maintenance date
monthly.fail: Arrange maintenance by a competent person

monthly.text: CO2 units: weight is within tolerance of the full weight on the label
Mounted securely. Top of units up to 18 kg (40 lb) no higher than 1.5 m (5 ft) from the floor (NFPA 10)

placement: Travel distance to a Class A extinguisher should be no more than 22.9 m (75 ft) under NFPA 10
Class B travel distance is 9 to 15 m (30 to 50 ft) depending on the hazard rating under NFPA 10
Put extinguishers on escape routes and near exits, not behind equipment
Place the right type at the hazard: CO2 or powder near electrical rooms, wet chemical in kitchens, foam near fuel stores
annual: Annual maintenance and tag by a competent person
Pressure or hydrostatic testing at the intervals in NFPA 10, EN 3 or the local rule and the manufacturer instructions
Keep a register: unit number, location, type, last service date, next due date

before: Valid hot work permit for this place and time
Remove or cover all combustibles within 11 m (35 ft), including below and behind the work
Cover floor and wall openings and cracks so sparks cannot pass through
Sprinklers in service. Extinguisher of the right type within reach
Test for flammable gas or vapour where needed and record it
Name a trained fire watch who knows the alarm and extinguisher use
during: Fire watch stays at the work area the whole time and has no other task
Watch the floors above, below and the other side of walls
Stop work at once if a spark lands on something that can burn
Keep communication to raise the alarm quickly
after: Fire watch continues for at least 30 minutes after work ends (NFPA 51B). Many sites require 60 minutes or more
Check hidden areas, ducts and the floor below for smouldering
Sign off on the permit only after the final check
Report any fire, however small, and review the cause
rules: No fire watch means no hot work
The fire watch must be able to see all spark areas. Use extra watchers if needed
Never leave a fire watch alone in a confined space

drill.frequency: At least once a year, or as required by local law, the site fire plan and the client. Include night shift and contractors.
before: Plan the scenario and the date. Tell management and the emergency services where required
Name the drill leader, timekeeper and observers
Check alarms, exits, assembly points and warden lists are ready
Brief the fire wardens on their duties
during: Sound the alarm and start the timer
Wardens sweep their areas and close doors
People leave by the nearest safe exit and do not use lifts
Everyone reports to the assembly point and wardens do the headcount
Record the time to clear the building and the time to complete the headcount
Observers note blocked exits, people ignoring the alarm and confusion
after: Hold a short debrief the same day
List findings: what worked, what failed, who was missing
Raise corrective actions with owners and dates in the Action Tracker
Record the drill: date, time, number of people, evacuation time, findings
Share the lessons with all workers and contractors
